messages.text: 你好，請問這篇論文在講什麼？我是在看老師推薦的額外閱讀，想先大概了解一下。

messages.short_answer: 這篇論文是 Miguel Sicart 的〈Defining Game Mechanics〉，主要在提出一個「遊戲機制（game mechanics）」的正式定義：機制是由「代理者（agents）」調用、為與遊戲狀態互動而設計的方法，並借用物件導向程式設計的概念。作者希望這個定義能用於形式化分析遊戲，並連結控制器設計與使用者體驗，最後以 Shadow of the Colossus、Rez 與 Every Extend Extra 進行比較分析。

sections.title: 論文要解決的問題
sections.text: 作者指出「遊戲機制」一詞在遊戲研究與設計中定義含混，並以 Gears of War 的掩體機制與極簡遊戲 Orbital 作為開場例子。作者認為既有定義缺乏足夠精確性，難以用於形式分析，特別是難以連結規則與機制，也難以辨識個別機制。

sections.title: 核心定義與論文架構
sections.text: 作者把機制定義為「由代理者調用、為與遊戲狀態互動而設計的方法」，並主張規則與機制在本體上有所區別：規則定義可能性空間並規範狀態轉換，機制則是互動方法。論文依序回顧既有定義、提出正式定義、討論核心／主要／次要機制，最後以三款遊戲作比較分析，並在結論反思定義的不足。

sections.title: 對實際應用的意義
sections.text: 作者認為此定義可協助描述與修改機制、改善遊戲設計文件，並促進設計師與程式設計師之間的溝通。作者也承認此定義並非終極定義，仍有許多灰色地帶未處理。

sections.title: 閱讀建議
sections.text: 若只想大致了解，可先讀前言與結論，掌握「機制是代理者調用的互動方法」這個核心想法；若有興趣的是實際應用，可再看第三部分對三款遊戲的比較分析。

sources.text: In this article, I propose a definition of game mechanics useful for the analysis of games and their formal constituents. This definition will allow for formalized analysis of game structures, and it will also open up for the possibility of connecting formal game analysis with research on controller designs and user experience. I define game mechanics, using concepts from object-oriented programming, as methods invoked by agents, designed for interaction with the game state. With this formalized definition, I intend to: Provide a tool to discover, describe, and interrelate game mechanics in any given game. Define mechanics also in relation to elements of the game system, game hardware and player experience, mapping mechanics to input procedures and player emotions. Even though I will be mentioning concepts like game rules, challenges, emotions and user experience, it is not my intention to enter the debate on those topics. Here, I use those concepts in a relational way: defining game mechanics requires mentioning and acknowledging rules, challenges and emotions.
quotes: I define game mechanics, using concepts from object-oriented programming, as methods invoked by agents, designed for interaction with the game state.

sources.text: The article by Miguel Sicart addresses the ambiguity of the term 'game mechanics' in game research and design, using the cover system in Gears of War and the minimalist game Orbital as opening examples. It proposes a formal definition that treats game mechanics, drawing on object-oriented programming concepts, as methods invoked by agents for interacting with the game state, defined in relation to rules, challenges and emotions used in an instrumental way. The introduction states the aims: to provide an analytical tool for describing game mechanics, to connect formal analysis with controller design and user experience, and to set up a comparative analysis of Shadow of the Colossus, Rez and Every Extend Extra. The pages also outline a plan that includes a review of previous definitions of mechanics, a discussion of primary and secondary mechanics, and a conclusion on the definition's shortcomings, though these later sections are not included in the text shown.

These pages review how game studies has analysed games through their formal elements, distinguishing systems, players, and player-system contexts. They trace the distinction between rules and mechanics from Avedon through Lundgren and Björk, Rouse, Fullerton et al., Cook, the MDA framework, and Järvinen. The authors argue that most prior definitions of game mechanics lack the precision needed for formal analysis, particularly in linking rules to mechanics and identifying individual mechanics. The pages also note that Järvinen's goal-oriented account struggles to explain sandbox play in games such as Sim City and Crackdown.

For designers and theorists, game mechanics are discrete units that can be created, analyzed and put in relation to others. But for any agent in a game, the mechanics is everything that affords agency in the game world. Mechanics is thus tied to agency in the game system. With this definition of game mechanics, I have intended to contribute to game studies by: Formalizing an ontological difference between rules and mechanics that can potentially lead to detailed game analysis, and Suggesting a mapping between game mechanics, input procedures, and player experience. This very formal definition still leaves some questions unanswered, especially with regards to well-known terminology such as core mechanics. In the next section, I present some further implications of this definition for the analysis of games. Interlude: Core, Primary and Secondary Mechanics Game design literature uses the "game mechanics" concept extensively, incorporating certain qualifiers to it. It is not rare to find in the literature notions like "core mechanics" (Järvinen, 2998, p. 255; Rollings and Adams, 2007, pp.

These pages define game mechanics as methods invoked by agents, designed for interaction with the game state, borrowing terminology from object-oriented programming. The author argues this definition is less anthropocentric than prior approaches, since mechanics can be invoked by human players, AI agents, or bots, with examples drawn from Shadow of the Colossus and Gears of War. The text also argues that the framework supports mapping mechanics to input devices, using UML-style modeling, and discusses how fighting-game mastery relates to input mapping. Finally, it introduces 'context mechanics' triggered by the player's situation in the game world, illustrated with Gears of War, Assassin's Creed and Wario Ware, Inc.; the author notes that studying bots' access to mechanics is outside the article's scope.

These pages from Sicart's article 'Defining Game Mechanics' argue for an ontological distinction between rules and mechanics: rules provide the possibility space and regulate state transitions, while mechanics are methods designed for interaction with the game state. The author illustrates this with Shadow of the Colossus, where climbing is a mechanic constrained by a stamina property derived from a rule, and the game loop evaluates interactions against those rules. The text also distinguishes designed gameplay from players' unpredictable uses, such as toyplay, noting that formal design cannot fully determine how a game is played. Finally, it begins an interlude on how qualifiers like core, primary and secondary mechanics fit the proposed definition, drawing on Salen and Zimmerman and Järvinen.

These pages come from a Game Studies article defining game mechanics, shifting from formal definition to application. The author compares Shadow of the Colossus, Rez and Every Extend Extra through their core input-based mechanics, arguing that each uses a tension-and-release structure. The stabbing mechanic in Shadow of the Colossus, the shoot mechanic in Rez and the explode mechanic in Every Extend Extra are read as design choices that shape intended player experiences such as powerlessness and epic achievement, or synaesthetic musical engagement. The section concludes that developers modified well-known core mechanics to alter player expectations and agency.

These pages conclude Sicart's article defining game mechanics as methods invoked by agents for interacting with the game world, drawing on object-oriented programming and game studies. They discuss practical uses of the definition: formally describing and modifying mechanics, improving game design documentation, and easing communication between designers and programmers. The conclusion argues that mechanics are performative while rules are normative, and that treating them as distinct is useful for analysing computer games. The author acknowledges that the definition is not the ultimate one, that many grey areas remain unexplored, and that no dominant definition of rules or mechanics exists in game studies. The pages end with acknowledgements and a reference list.

Conclusion This article was born out of necessity: having an analytical vocabulary for defining game structures and systems that allowed a formal, precise, and scalable description of games as systems and how they interrelate with player practices. The result of this necessity is a formal definition of game mechanics that owes to object-oriented programming its formal phrasing, while inheriting from game studies the figure of players, or agents, as fundamental to understand how games are designed and played. This article has defined game mechanics as methods invoked by agents for interacting with the game world. This definition allows the study of the systemic structure of games in terms of actions afforded to agents to overcome challenges, but also the analysis of how actions are mapped onto input devices and how mechanics can be used to create specific emotional experiences in players. There are, however, many grey areas I do not have the space to focus on here. Perhaps the most significant is the ontological distinction between rules and mechanics. Game researchers have argued convincingly that mechanics could be understood as subsets of rules.
quotes: Game researchers have argued convincingly that mechanics could be understood as subsets of rules.

I do so in an instrumental way and leave for further research the implications of this definition for understanding other systemic components of games. Since both game researchers and game designers have covered the topic of game mechanics, I begin this article with an analytical summary of the major works on this topic, providing a general overview of these previous definitions of game mechanics and place my work within this tradition. The second part of this article presents the definition of game mechanics, detailing the elements that compose it. I then present a brief reflection on primary and secondary mechanics and how they can be derived from this definition. These concepts are put into practice in the third part, where I perform a comparative analysis of Shadow of the Colossus (Team Ico, 2005), Rez (United Game Artists, 2002), and Every Extend Extra (Q Entertainment, 2006), highlighting the use of this concept of mechanics in the research on game structure and user experience.

messages.short_answer: 大致可以這樣理解，但不完全等同於「玩家按按鈕」。作者把遊戲機制定義為「由代理者調用、為與遊戲狀態互動而設計的方法」。代理者不只是人類玩家，電腦系統或 AI（例如 bots）也可以是代理者；機制是代理者在規則所劃定的可能性空間中能採取的行動。按鍵與輸入裝置的對應，是論文另外討論的「機制與輸入程序、玩家體驗之間的對應」。

sections.title: 定義的三個關鍵詞
sections.text: 論文先給出定義：遊戲機制是由代理者調用的方法，並且是為了與遊戲狀態互動而設計。作者說明「methods invoked by agents」是借用物件導向程式設計的術語，把遊戲中的行動類比為方法，把行動者類比為呼叫方法的一方。

sections.title: 機制與規則、代理者的關係
sections.text: 作者指出，規則提供機制可以發生的可能性空間，規則是為代理者而建模，機制則是為代理者的行動而設計。對一般代理者而言，機制就是所有能讓它在遊戲世界中行動的東西。

sections.title: 用一個比喻幫助理解
sections.text: 可以把遊戲想像成一個系統，「機制」像是系統裡可以被呼叫的動作，例如跳躍、射擊；「代理者」則是呼叫這些動作的人或電腦程式。按鍵只是讓人類玩家觸發動作的一種方式，論文關心的是動作本身，以及它如何影響遊戲狀態。這是我的說明，論文並未用按鈕來比喻。

In the following section I present a formal definition of game mechanics, together with the arguments that make it a more precise and inclusive approach than those reviewed in this section. Defining Game Mechanics Let's start with a definition: game mechanics are methods invoked by agents, designed for interaction with the game state. The different components of this definition require further explanation: "Methods invoked by agents" defines this approach to game mechanics, as it formalizes the use of terminology taken from the object oriented programming paradigm (Weisfeld, 2000). In this appropriation of the terminology, object orientation provides a set of metaphors that describe the elements of systems and their interrelations. I do not want to imply that the analysis of the source code of a game will reveal that all game mechanics have been implemented as methods of classes or that object-oriented programming should be considered a default methodology for the actual production of computer games. Nor am I implying that the Object Oriented Framework should be extended to a formal analysis of all elements of the game.
quotes: Let's start with a definition: game mechanics are methods invoked by agents, designed for interaction with the game state.

All of these are methods for agency within the game world, actions the player can take within the space of possibility created by the rules. On occasion, those methods will be other than the ones made available to the human player, which can have consequences worth of analysis. sources.text: Implicit in this definition is an ontological difference between rules and mechanics. Game mechanics are concerned with the actual interaction with the game state, while rules provide the possibility space where that interaction is possible, regulating as well the transition between states. In this sense, rules are modeled after agency, while mechanics are modeled for agency. In this object oriented framework, rules could be considered general or particular properties of the game system and its agents. All objects in games have properties. These properties are often either rules or determined by rules. These rules are evaluated by a game loop, an algorithm that relates the current state of the game and the properties of the objects with a number of conditions that consequently can modify the game state. For example, the winning condition, the losing condition and the effects of action in the player's avatar health are calculated when running the game loop. This algorithm relates rules with mechanics, exemplifying the applicability of an ontological distinction between rules and mechanics.

sections.title: 論文如何區分規則與機制
sections.text: 作者指出，機制關注的是與遊戲狀態的實際互動，而規則提供互動得以發生的可能性空間，並規範狀態之間的轉換。作者因此說規則是依據能動性（agency）建模的，機制則是為能動性而建模的。作者也指出，規則具有規範性，機制則具有表演性（performative）。

sections.title: 你的理解與論文提到的另一種觀點
sections.text: 論文提到，有些研究（如 Lundgren 和 Björk）把機制視為規則的一部分，也就是低層次的規則描述或規則群集，因此不需要在規則與機制之間做定義上的區分。作者並不同意把兩者完全等同，而是主張區分有助於更清楚地描述遊戲分析。

sections.title: 用規則手冊與實際行動來理解（舉例，非論文內容）
sections.text: 可以想像一本遊戲的規則手冊：它說明哪些行動可行、哪些狀態會導致勝負。機制則像是玩家在這套規則允許的範圍內，實際執行的互動，例如在《Shadow of the Colossus》中攀爬、跳躍或射箭。這個比喻只是幫助理解，論文本身並未使用這個例子。

sources.text: 11). Some formalist approaches makes a difference between the rules of the game and the actions afforded to players by those rules. This conceptual perspective can be tracked back to Avedon (1971) who suggests a formal structure of games in which there are "specific operations, required courses of action, method of play," which he defines as the "procedure for action", as opposed to the "rules governing action", which are "fixed principles that determine conduct and standards for behavior" (p. 422). However, this formal distinction between rules and mechanics is not always applied in game mechanics research. Lundgren and Björk (2003) define game mechanics as "any part of the rule system of a game that covers one, and only one, possible kind of interaction that takes place during the game, be it general or specific (...) mechanics are regarded as a way to summarize game rules". In this view, mechanics is a term that encompasses those rules that are applied when the player interacts with the game, and there is no need for a definitional distinction between rules and mechanics. Game mechanics would be low-level descriptions of game rules or clusters of game rules.

sections.title: 用這個定義判斷跳躍
sections.text: 如果把「跳躍」理解為玩家（代理者）調用的動作，它符合機制的定義。至於「只能在地面或某些條件下跳」這類限制，則比較接近論文所說會約束機制的規則，例如論文用 stamina 門檻限制攀爬的例子。

sections.title: 機制與規則的分工（舉例，非論文內容）
sections.text: 假設角色只能在踩到地面時起跳，「按下跳躍鍵後角色跳起」是機制，「必須在地面上才能起跳」則是規則。這只是用來幫助理解的假設例子，並非論文內容。

sections.title: 目前文本的限制
sections.text: 目前檢索到的段落沒有討論平台遊戲或跳躍的具體設計，因此上述判斷只能依據論文的一般定義與 Shadow of the Colossus 的例子推論。若要確認，最好再查看論文是否討論過規則與機制在其他遊戲類型中的界線。

sources.text: A game mechanic, then, is the action invoked by an agent to interact with the game world, as constrained by the game rules. In Gears of War, if the player wants to take cover, she has to press the A button in the controller. This will make the avatar seek cover in the closest environment object that can provide that cover. In that sense, a mechanic is limited by the rules that apply to the gameworld (the general physics simulations, for instance, whose objects are suitable for providing some kind of cover), and, on occasion, to rules that apply exclusively to that particular mechanic - for example, some mechanics can only be invoked in certain environments or gameplay contexts. Following Järvinen (2008), the best way of understanding mechanics as methods is to formalize them as verbs, with other syntactical/structural elements, such as rules, having influence on how those verbs act in the game. For example, in Shadow of the Colossus we find the following mechanics: to climb, ride (the horse), stab, jump, shoot (arrows), whistle, grab, run (and variations like swim or dive).
quotes: A game mechanic, then, is the action invoked by an agent to interact with the game world, as constrained by the game rules.

sources.text: For example, in Shadow of the Colossus we find the following mechanics: to climb, ride (the horse), stab, jump, shoot (arrows), whistle, grab, run (and variations like swim or dive). In Gears of War, a noncomprehensive list would be: cover, shoot, reload, throw (grenade), look (at a point of interest), use, give orders, switch weapons[2]. All of these are methods for agency within the game world, actions the player can take within the space of possibility created by the rules. This definition departs from the implicit anthropocentrism of previous approaches. Game mechanics can be invoked by any 2026/9/5 15:03 Game Studies - Defining Game Mechanics https://gamestudies.org/0802/articles/sicart 5/16 agent, be that human or part of the computer system. For instance, AI agents also have a number of methods available to interact with the gameworld. On occasion, those methods will be other than the ones made available to the human player, which can have consequences worth of analysis. This approach can be particularly interesting when trying to understand the effect of bots in MMORPGs, since bots are agents that optimize their interaction by focusing on a core set of mechanics.
quotes: For example, in Shadow of the Colossus we find the following mechanics: to climb, ride (the horse), stab, jump, shoot (arrows), whistle, grab, run (and variations like swim or dive).

sources.text: This algorithm relates rules with mechanics, exemplifying the applicability of an ontological distinction between rules and mechanics. For example, in Shadow of the Colossus players have a game mechanic called "climb", but they are also determined by a property called "stamina", which is the algorithmic translation of a rule: "players have x stamina units". The climbing mechanic states that when invoked, stamina is lost at a certain ratio. A property/rule states that if stamina is below a certain threshold, climbing is not possible anymore. The game loop checks the game state; if the player invokes the climb mechanic, those functions that determine the consequences and boundaries of the players' interaction are called, and the resulting changes in the game state are evaluated against the rules of the game. Then, the player will succeed or not in "climbing", depending on their "stamina". The second part of the definition claims that game mechanics are methods "designed for interaction with the game state". This implies that the task of game designers is to create mechanics that agents can use to interact with the game. These interactions modify the game state (Juul, 2005, 59-64).
quotes: A property/rule states that if stamina is below a certain threshold, climbing is not possible anymore.

persona_text:
# Persona: Mei

**Who.** Mei is a third-year undergraduate from Taiwan taking a game design course, and a non-native
English speaker. A topic from the lecture caught her interest, so she is reading the teacher's extra
readings on her own.

**What she wants.** To understand the main ideas well enough to explain them and connect them to the
lecture. She has no research project. Reading goal: *Get a general overview of this paper*.

**How she behaves.**
- Writes in Traditional Chinese (繁體字). Interface language: 中文（繁體）.
- Has limited background. Starts with broad questions ("這篇在講什麼？"), then asks for basic definitions.
- Often restates an idea in her own words to check her understanding, and is sometimes wrong (e.g. mixes up
  mechanics and dynamics, or treats a game mechanic as the same thing as a rule or a goal).
- Says plainly when she still does not understand ("還是不太懂", "可以換個方式解釋嗎？").
- Tends to accept answers and rarely opens the sources unless prompted.
- Brings in examples from games she plays or from the lecture and asks whether they fit the paper.

**Papers.** MDA: A Formal Approach to Game Design and Game Research; Game Studies – Defining Game Mechanics.
